correctness.rationale: Each good has ONE Bernoulli(p) common realized utility for every agent, independently across goods. Precommitted disjoint bundles produce independent Bin(k_i,p) success counts; realized EF1 is exactly range<=1. Transfer one Bernoulli from size b to a (b>=a+2), couple U~Bin(a,p), V~Bin(b-1,p) and apply antisymmetry plus monotone-likelihood-ratio order. The (U,V)=(0,1) all-other-zero event yields strict gain >=(b-a-1)p²(1-p)^(m-2). Iterated smoothing gives unique balanced bundle multiset, finite adjacent-interval inclusion-exclusion yields exact P*, and the binomial local CLT/Gaussian Riemann sum gives (2^n-1)/sqrt(n)*(2π q p(1-p))^(-(n-1)/2) for fixed n,p. The m<=n and n=2 boundaries are covered. Independent exact exhaustive small-allocation enumeration agrees.

value.rationale: PASS. The gap between ex-ante fairness and ex-post EF1 is a natural risk-of-fairness question; this theorem classifies every optimal pre-realization assignment, gives a sharp positive one-transfer improvement for all population and goods counts, and proves that even optimal eventual realized fairness decays polynomially with exact coefficient. It is an independently useful stochastic fair-division result beyond an elementary binary event probability.

limitations: One binary realized good value shared identically by agents; fixed ex-ante allocation; iid p in (0,1); fixed n,p asymptotic. Does not claim agent-specific or heterogeneous probabilities.
